data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman name Sergius, meaning 'protector' or 'servant.' In Christian tradition, Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus are celebrated as a pair, and their feast day is on January 3. The name Sergio carries the meaning “Sergeant, Leader” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Sergio usually hope their child will grow to embody sergeant, leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sergio total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_greek.name: Σέργιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὀνοματολογίαν με ελληνική ρίζα το όνομα Σέργιος προέρχεται από το Σέργιον (Σέργιος, Σέργιον), που σημαίνει «Ελπίδα στερεά». Ο Σέργιος ήταν ένα από τα πιο δημοφιλή ονόματα στην Αρχαία Ελλάδα, και συνδέεται με το μύθο του Σέργιου, που ήταν ο εραστής της Αφροδίτης.

This name has been popular throughout history in various Western cultures, and it continues to resonate today, especially among individuals who aspire to be selfless protectors, mentors, and leaders.
data.spiritual_significance: For Christians, the name Sergio holds spiritual significance as it draws inspiration from Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus. These saints are revered for their dedication to their faith and unwavering commitment to helping those in need. The name Sergio is a constant reminder of the importance of living a life rooted in love, compassion, and service to others. By embracing this name, individuals can strive to embody the courage, humility, and selflessness that Saint Sergius and Saint Bacchus exhibited throughout their lives.

historical_references.reference: Saint Sergius of Resafim and Borgoy, also known as Saint Sergius of Radonezh, was a Russian Orthodox monk and hegumen of the Trinity-Saint Sergius Lavra in Russia. Born around 1314 in the village of Radonezh, he is venerated as a patron saint of Russia. He lived during the late 14th century.

Saint Sergius of Thiesos, also known as Sergius of Stagnum, was a Cappadocian Greek monk and bishop. He is traditionally believed to have lived during the late 5th and early 6th centuries. Sergius and his companions are considered the founders of the monastic tradition in the Mediterranean world, and he is often referred to as the 'Father of Monasticism in the West'.
